title: Closing-Hold
primitive: the last word — the small specific image that lets the listener carry the tale away
summary: The Close beat is the only beat the listener LEAVES with. A weak Close evaporates; a strong Close stays in the room after the teller stops talking. This kit listens for what the kid actually puts in their last sentence — and whether it echoes anything from the Hook. Phase 2 makes the Close the most-deliberate beat in the tale.

questions.prompt: Tell a 60-second tale and pay close attention to your very last sentence. Was it a SPECIFIC image (something a listener could draw) or a SUMMARY (something a listener could only paraphrase)? Specific images stay. Summaries evaporate.
What's the strongest move for a Close beat the listener will carry into tomorrow?
options: End with a moral — tell the listener what the tale meant.
End with a small specific image that echoes something from the Hook.
End with a cliffhanger — make them want a sequel.
questions.rationale: A Close that echoes the Hook gives the tale a SHAPE — the listener feels they have arrived back at a place they've already been, but with new eyes. Morals tell the listener what to feel; cliffhangers leave the room open instead of closing it.

questions.prompt: Look at the last sentence of three tales in your anthology. Which one stays with you the longest? What is it about that one — is it specific, does it echo the Hook, does it leave a small image you can SEE?

Take a tale that ended with a summary or a moral. Rewrite ONLY the last sentence — replace it with a small specific image that echoes one detail from the Hook. Keep everything in between identical. Read both versions aloud.

castCameos.line: The Close is a refrain. The Hook plants the chord; the Close lets it ring. The tale is a song that closes the loop.
Specific Close-beat images are what I lean toward when I think of the tale tomorrow. Summaries get filed; specifics get RE-told.
A great Close shows the listener that the rotation at the Turn STAYED rotated. The tale is different from how it started — the Close proves it.
Slow your very last sentence. Let the room hold it. The Close is the only sentence that's allowed to be longer than it needs to be.
